title: Morpho market exposure is capped in two dimensions at once — an absolute size and a relative share
content:
The Morpho USDT instance's `Market Exposure` block (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.4.3.1.1.4.1) lists each lending pool with three fields: a Pool ID, an **Absolute cap**, and a **Relative cap**. The wstETH/USDT 86% LLTV pool gets 250 million absolute / 100% relative; WBTC/USDT gets 100 million / 100%; cbBTC/USDT gets 250 million / 100%.

Two caps rather than one is the design point. An absolute cap bounds the loss from a single pool failing. A relative cap bounds *concentration* — what fraction of the instance's assets may sit in one market — which is the quantity that matters when the instance itself grows or shrinks. Whichever binds first governs.

Without the relative dimension, a fixed notional cap becomes progressively more permissive as the instance shrinks: 250 million is a modest slice of a large vault and the entire vault when the vault is small. Without the absolute dimension, a percentage cap scales the exposure to a single collateral type without limit as deposits grow.

Here all three capped pools are set to 100% relative, meaning the concentration lever is present but not currently engaged — only the notional caps bind. The mechanism is available; the current configuration declines to use half of it.
description: Each pool carries both an absolute cap and a relative cap, so a limit can bind on notional size or on portfolio concentration, whichever binds first.
